title: Equation-Consistency Gated Reflection for Small Language Models: A Training-Free Approach to Preventing Self-Correction Regressions

contributions.purpose: Characterize the harm of naive self-reflection for small LLMs on math reasoning.
contributions.mechanism: Measure accuracy and correct-to-incorrect regressions when Llama-3-8B-Instruct performs naive self-reflection on GSM8K.
contributions.evaluation: Accuracy drops 24.4 percentage points on GSM8K (79.68% -> 55.27%), with 36.25% of originally correct answers regressing to incorrect.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that naive self-reflection is harmful for small LLMs on mathematical reasoning, with accuracy dropping 24.4pp on GSM8K and 36.25% of correct answers regressing to incorrect.

contributions.purpose: Prevent harmful self-correction regressions without training.
contributions.mechanism: Propose ECGR, a training-free gate that extracts arithmetic equations from original and revised solutions, verifies them with SymPy, and selects the solution with higher consistency score.
contributions.evaluation: Reduces correct-to-incorrect (c->i) regression rates by over 92% on both GSM8K and GSM-Plus (from 36.25% to 2.76% on GSM8K).
contributions.source_quote: We propose ECGR, a training-free gating mechanism that reduces correct-to-incorrect (c->i) regression rates by over 92% on both GSM8K and GSM-Plus, from 36.25% to 2.76% on GSM8K.

contributions.purpose: Identify the main limitation of the method.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze equation coverage, the fraction of solutions containing checkable arithmetic equations.
contributions.evaluation: Low equation coverage (~43%) is the key bottleneck limiting ECGR's practical gains over simpler baselines like self-consistency.
contributions.source_quote: We identify equation coverage (~43%) as the key bottleneck limiting ECGR's practical gains, providing insights for future work on verification-guided self-correction.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work addresses this challenge by introducing a deterministic verification mechanism that gates self-reflection output, preventing the harmful regressions observed in naive self-correction approaches.

Our approach differs by using lightweight symbolic verification (SymPy) to check equation consistency without requiring trained reward models or program execution, making it training-free and computationally efficient.

notes: Mixed result with a self-flagged limitation: ECGR strongly reduces regressions (c->i down >92%) but the authors note low equation coverage (~43%) limits practical gains over simpler baselines like self-consistency.
